Opens the window, or full screen mode, that 3D programs are drawn in. It has to be the first graphics command of a 3D program: every other 3D command fails until it ran. After it, the back buffer is the target of drawing and you draw one frame at a time with [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and [Flip](Flip).

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 0 | Window while testing and full screen otherwise. This is the default. |
| 1 | Full screen. |
| 2 | Window. |
| 3 | Window whose size can be changed by the user; the picture is scaled to fit. |
| 4 | Window without a border: no title bar and no frame. This is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. |

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity cube, 1, 2, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```
@param width  Width of the picture in pixels.
@param height  Height of the picture in pixels.
@param depth  Color depth: 0 for the best, or 16, 24 or 32. Defaults to 0.
@param mode  Window or full screen as in the table. Defaults to 0.
@gap The depth is ignored: the picture always has at least 8 bits each of red, green and blue (with 8 bits of alpha where it is used), because palette and 16 bit rendering are not supported.
@gap Full screen (mode 1) does not change the video mode of the display: the picture is shown at the largest size that fits with its aspect ratio kept, and the rest is black. See [Fullscreen](Fullscreen).
@gap A window without a border (mode 4) has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.
